page: Amazon Web Services c5d.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and Intel Xeon 8275CL x86_64 processors. Operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz, the platform provides 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is provisioned at 192.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. For local I/O requirements, the instance bundles 3600 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core processing and high data throughput. Multi-threaded evaluations, including stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU benchmarks, place the instance in the top quartile of performance. Vector computation capabilities, assisted by AVX-512 extensions, drive strong results in Geekbench Clang compilation and ray tracing. Memory subsystems deliver an uncached read bandwidth of 231.4 GB/sec and an uncached write bandwidth of 97.89 GB/sec. Application testing shows strong database operations in Passmark, static web serving throughput of 45.17 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput exceeding 81 million operations per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances high compute density with dense local solid-state storage. By integrating 3600 GB of direct NVMe capacity, it eliminates reliance on remote network storage for scratch data, log parsing, or local indexing. The primary performance limitation is single-thread execution, where benchmarks such as single-core stress-ng and Geekbench register middle-tier scores. Furthermore, the absence of hardware accelerators makes the platform inefficient for machine learning text generation, where tokens-per-second benchmarks reflect weak throughput.

The c5d.24xlarge is engineered for compute-heavy applications that demand fast local disk access. Best-fit deployments include distributed cache nodes, parallel software build and CI/CD clusters, batch media encoding, ray tracing, and static web traffic delivery. It also effectively supports data preprocessing and analytical workloads that fit within its 192 GB memory footprint while benefiting from high-throughput local disk storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 3.6 GHz. It includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 3600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a 25 Gbps baseline network throughput. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core performance across stress-ng, Passmark CPU tests, and software compilation via Clang, alongside high memory bandwidth and top-tier Redis SET execution at 81.12 million operations per second. However, single-core metrics remain average, and text generation speeds for large language models are weak due to the absence of dedicated GPUs. The c5d.24xlarge provides high resource density for parallel compute tasks, making it a reliable solution for compilation pipelines, ray tracing, batch computation, static web serving, and database workloads requiring high local I/O.
